newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on regional demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel prices firmed at midday Friday on fresh regional demand with the spread or regrade widening, traders said.
January gas oil was last traded at $32.20 per barrel, up sharply from Thursday's $31.75/$32.25, brokers said.

Traders said firmer prices were due to buying interest from China and strong demand from South Asia where India, Nepal and Sri Lanka have all issued purchase tenders for January and February gas oil and jet fuel.
As a result of this new demand the January regrade widened to $2.00/$2.50 per barrel from Thursday's $1.90/$2.10. January traded on late Thursday at $2.00 per barrel, brokers said.
February was quoted at $1.80/$2.55 from $1.50/$1.90 per barrel.
India has issused a second February tender to buy up to 45,000 tonnes of gas oil after having already purchased a total volume of around 720,000 tonnes.
Cash gas oil prices was last quoted at $32.00/$32.20 a barrel for January loading supplies.
"Gas oil sentiment is currently very firm. Besides India there were also demand from Nepal and Sri Lanka," said a trader.
Firm crude levels have also provided some support.
NYMEX February crude was last traded on ACCESS at $25.16, up 24 cents from overnight New York after API data showed a 6.1 million barrel draw in crude stocks.
The API also showed a 1.5 million barrel draw in distillate stocks. But some traders said the draw disguised a 284,000 barrel build in heating oil stocks.
January fuel oil was steady in quiet trading and was quoted at $121/$122 per tonne.
